chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Ismā'īl ibn Najīḥ al-Rammāḥ who said:
We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina on one of the nights, so he said: 'What are these people saying regarding [the verse]
So whoever hastens [his departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him

So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him for the one who fears [God]. It is for you all, and the people are the multitude, and you are the pilgrims.

key_terms.لِمَنِ اتَّقَى: For the one who fears God (taqwa)
key_terms.يَوْمَيْنِ: Two days (referring to the 11th and 12th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Who is permitted to leave Mina early or stay late during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevailing view that the Quranic permission for hastening or delaying departure from Mina was restricted by social status—specifically, that it applied only to Bedouins or city dwellers respectively. He clarifies that the phrase 'for those who fear' (liman ittaqa) refers to all pilgrims, establishing that the flexibility in timing is a universal concession for the entire community of Hajj, regardless of their background.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Ismail, Bin Najeeh Al Rammah who said,
‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in Mina on a night from the night, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What are they (people) saying regarding

[2:203] then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him?’ We said, ‘We do not know’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, they are saying, ‘The one who hastens, from the people of the valleys, so there is no sin upon him, and the one who delays, from the people of the urban areas, so there is no sin upon him’; and it is not as they are saying it to be.

Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise Says [2:203] then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, indeed there is no sin upon him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him, indeed there is no sin upon him for the one who fears. But rather, it is for you all, and the people are the multitude, and you are the pilgrims’.
en.sarwar: 12. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab from ‘Isma’il ibn al-Najih al-Rammah who has said the following: “During one of the nights we were with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in Mina’.

He (the Imam) asked, ‘What do these people say about, “Those who depart in the second day for departure, there is no sin on them and those who delay, there is no sin on them?”’ [2:203] We replied, ‘We do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, they say that those of the people of wilderness who depart in a hurry have not committed a sin, and those of the people of the cities who delay have not committed a sin.’ It is not as they say it is.
Allah, most glorious is whose praise has said, “On those who depart earlier in the second day for departure, there is no sin.”

You must take notice; there no sin remains on those who leave early as well as on those who delay. You must take notice that no sin remains on them. They are only those ones who maintain piety before Allah. This applies to you only. People are the crowd and you are the ones who have performed al-Hajj.’” (Fatwa best explains Hadith 11 of this Chapter and all of the following Chapter)
